checked.item: PT-only / QBO-only / Pro+ only / per-integration / requires Apply-payments-to-invoices on / new overlay entry point — scope_of_iteration_1
Apply payments toggle gates access to the matching-rules entry button (R20, R23)
'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' is one stored value shown on both the overlay and GSP (R18)
Two modes: default matching (non-editable reference info) vs custom rules (R2, R20)
Exactly three scope rows: Customer, Invoice date, Invoice-number match; no locked Balance>0/open-invoices row (R2)
Invoice-number scope row offers only the 4 QBO-query operands, default 'is equal to' (R4)
Invoice-number scope row target is always DocNumber (R6)
Selectable source fields: Invoice number, Invoice note, Invoice id, Subscription id, Invoice metadata, Payment note, Payment metadata (R7)
Scope validity guard: at most one of Customer/Invoice-number off, exact blocking copy (R8)
Customer inheritance available and required when the Customer scope row is off (R9)
Metadata source with no key blocks save with a specific message (R10)
Invoice date off = no date limit, admin-gated, off-switch disabled otherwise (R11)
21-character DocNumber truncation stated on the field (R13)
Condition box offers all 10 operands (R5)
Condition rows target DocNumber or PrivateNote only (R6)
One AND/OR combinator for the whole box; row order is not a combinator (R12)
No configuration pre-filled on first entry to a state (R20)

findings.element: Custom rules panel — Customer scope row
findings.finding: Nowhere in the custom rules panel does a 'customer inheritance' setting appear, even though the Customer scope row's enable checkbox can be unchecked.
findings.user_impact: A user can disable the Customer scope with no way to configure how the payment's customer gets decided, leaving the core matching rule underspecified for that combination.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the customer-inheritance control (required, blocking save when off) and surface it whenever the Customer scope row is disabled.

evidence.quote: Customer inheritance ('a payment that matches an invoice takes its customer from that invoice') is available AND REQUIRED only when the Customer scope row is off. Saving with Customer off and inheritance off must be blocked.

findings.element: Matching rules overlay — no 'Cancel sync' control
findings.finding: 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' exists only on the GSP Invoices page; the overlay never shows or lets the user change it, and the code explicitly avoids writing it from the overlay.
findings.user_impact: A user configuring matching rules inside the overlay has no visibility into or control over the cancel-on-no-match behaviour without leaving the overlay.
findings.suggested_fix: Surface the single stored cancel-sync value inside the overlay as well, editable from either surface.

evidence.quote: 'Cancel sync if there is no matching open invoice found for a payment' is ONE stored value shown on both the overlay and GSP; either surface can change it and the other inherits. Not a second copy.

findings.element: Then refine section, immediately after selecting 'Use custom rules'
findings.finding: Switching to 'Use custom rules' for the first time auto-populates two refine conditions (Invoice note contains Memo on statement; Payment note contains Memo on statement) instead of starting empty.
findings.user_impact: Two conditions the user never added silently narrow which invoices match, and a first-time user may not notice they exist or that they affect results.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the 'Then refine' list empty when custom mode is first selected; only populate rows via '+ Add condition'.

evidence.quote: S1.1: on first open the engine is off, the default matching behaviour is displayed as NON-EDITABLE reference information, and no configuration is pre-filled.

findings.element: Metadata key field error / submit banner
findings.finding: The metadata-key validation shows the generic 'Required' label and a generic 'Fix the highlighted fields' banner instead of the FDD's specified blocking message.
findings.user_impact: Users get generic validation copy instead of the specific guidance the spec calls for on this exact error.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the key-field/submit error copy with 'Enter the metadata key to match on.' for this case.

evidence.source: FDD SD-16243 Iteration 1, R10 (specified text: "Enter the metadata key to match on.")

findings.element: Toast — save confirmation on the overlay
findings.finding: The save-success toast reads 'Matching rules updated' without the exclamation mark the canonical Success toast pattern requires for update confirmations.
findings.user_impact: Copy is inconsistent with the product's established success-toast language, which is a stated canonical reference for this UI.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the toast text to 'Matching rules updated!' to match the canonical Success pattern.

gaps: gsp settings switch: with Apply payments off, the entry button becomes unavailable, so the overlay's required 'payments are not being applied' disclosure (R23) was never directly viewed in that state — only inferred from the plain-terms code path.
Plan-gating (below Pro, R22) was never exercised in the state map; the non-configurable state and its plan-requirement messaging could not be checked.

R1 (override/no-fallback), R3 (sort order), R14 (absent vs empty), R15–R17 (outcome/snapshot behaviour) are backend matching-engine semantics not observable from a static UI recon and were not exercised.

Close (×) and Escape-key paths were exercised, but no interaction that reaches a genuinely dirty, then-committed state was recorded, so whether 'Update' actually persists a full custom configuration end-to-end is unconfirmed from the state map alone.
reference_gaps: FDD is silent on Escape-key / discard-prompt behaviour for the overlay's close interaction, so the prototype's silent-discard-on-close cannot be scored as a fidelity finding.
R24/Q4 (Generic customer): the FDD marks the required behaviour as an open question, so the prototype's total silence on Generic customer cannot be scored as missing vs. a resolved reference.
Q3 (default finite N, self-serve maximum N, snapshot ceiling) is unresolved in the FDD, so the prototype's 90-day default and 3650-day max cannot be judged against a resolved number.
R27: the FDD explicitly states it does not supply a marketable name, so the prototype's chosen overlay title 'Payment matching rules' cannot be judged against a spec name.
